newsitem.title: GERMANY: German building union commission accepts pay deal.
newsitem.headline: German building union commission accepts pay deal.

text.p: The wages commission of German construction union IG Bau has agreed to a pay settlement reached in talks with employers on Friday, union sources said.
The commission is made of up regional union representatives and its approval is needed for any deal to be finally accepted.
Sources close to the commission said on Friday the compromise, which offers better sick pay benefit than an earlier proposed deal, had been accepted by a large majority.
"That means a strike in the construction industry has been averted," one source told Reuters after the commission ended its meeting in Frankfurt.
IG Bau has called a news conference for 1200 GMT to announce details of the agreement.

The deal cuts pay for the first three days of sickness to 80 percent of full pay whereas an earlier agreement reached after arbitration talks planned to cut sick pay for the first three weeks of illness.
The commission had on Monday rejected that agreement, prompting further negotiations.
In return, holiday bonuses will be reduced to 25 percent of monthly pay from 30 percent. Both employers' federations have already agreed to the pact.
